userManual.title: Tariff Workbench — How It Works
userManual.intro: Tariff Workbench defines versioned water supply tariff headers by financial year, connection type, category, and billing method for water demand calculation.
userManual.tariffConfigSub: Code, Name, FY, Type, Category, Method, Dates
userManual.point1Desc: – Defines Tariff Code, Name, Financial Year, Connection Type (Residential/Commercial), Connection Category (Regular/Flat/Annual), Billing Method (Metered/Slab/Flat), Effective From & To dates, and Active status.
userManual.point2Desc: – Version No tracks tariff iterations over time. New versions can be created for subsequent effective periods without overwriting historical tariff records.
userManual.point3Desc: – Tracks Draft or Published status. Published tariffs used in active billing demand generation are protected from destructive overwrites to ensure billing integrity.
userManual.noteTitle: Always create a new version or effective period
userManual.noteDesc: , then update parameters that reference them — published tariffs cannot be directly edited if used in demand generation.

detailView.safePublishingDesc: Draft → Validate overlapping dates/slabs → Preview sample bill → Publish → Lock. Once a demand references a rate snapshot, preserve historical tariff and publish a new version for future periods.
